text:
Situation: Sodium chloride injection products are on FDA's drug shortage list. FDA first posted the sodium acetate shortage on 2015-02-17 and it remains current as of 2026-10-21. Our inventory shows sodium chloride 0.9% 125 mL syringes at 10.2 days, sodium chloride 9 mg/mL at 9.2 days (Corvale East), and 16.7 days (Corvale Lakeside). General stores show sodium chloride ranging from 8.9 to 14.4 days across multiple entries.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage posting for sodium acetate began 2015-02-17 and is still current. An import alert 66-40 was published 2014-04-10. Fresenius Kabi plant FEI 3001833549 received an OAI classification after an inspection ending 2013-01-11 and a Warning Letter on 2012-02-22. Another Fresenius Kabi plant FEI 3006028606 received an OAI classification after an inspection ending 2016-01-19. The rule-selected alternate manufacturer is Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today.

Our position: Current sodium chloride stock is below 15 days at several sites. The long-standing FDA shortage posting and associated manufacturing compliance history indicate continued supply risk. We must secure alternative sources now.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to initiate purchase agreements with Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (not on FDA shortage list) — requires P&T committee approval.
2. Buyer to qualify Medefil, Inc. as secondary source (not on FDA shortage list) — requires P&T committee approval.
3. Buyer to evaluate Sandoz Inc. and Samson Medical Technologies, L.L.C. for contract addition (not on FDA shortage list) — requires P&T committee approval.

Not recommended: No clinical protocol changes; those are for treating clinicians and the committee. No single-source reliance on current Fresenius Kabi supply given compliance history.
